fields.name: field_0
fields.evidence: Storage set-up bg3.exe+0xE25200 registers an 8-byte slot with the destructor FUN_140591900, which frees the pointer held in the slot (GlobalAllocator::Free(*slot)) without destroying anything inside: the slot holds a heap object, and the object's member is not owned. Registry totalSize 16 = 8-byte object + 8. bg3.exe+0x2D6CC70 (~ Toolkit ls::StaticLevelPhysicsComponent::GetPhysicsFilePath, only user of 'StaticPhysics') reads the component's first qword as a pointer and the qword it points to as the level/resource record (STDString array at +0x10/+0x1C, FixedString at +8) to build '<path>/StaticPhysics/<name>'; Toolkit GetUniqueKey returns (**this) + 0xC. macOS default constructor stores one zero qword in the allocated object.

fields.name: _Pad8
fields.evidence: The registry size (16, client and server) is 8 bytes larger than the 8-byte object, the convention of the pointer-stored objects already declared (layouts/alive/ecl.CullTrigger.json); nothing writes it.

Not seen alive; the creator of the component was not found (only the generic set-up and add/remove handlers bg3.exe+0x2D6E2D0 / bg3.exe+0x2D6E0F0).
second_pass: The Windows set-up bg3.exe+0xE25200 (8-byte slot, destructor frees the slot's pointer) and the registry's 16 show a heap object of one qword, which bg3.exe+0x2D6CC70 dereferences as a pointer to the level physics record; size set to 16 with class_size 8 and an 8-byte tail (convention of the confirmed trigger layouts), fixing the raw-check size mismatch.
